title: Command Palette reinstalls with every PowerToys update, despite being deactivated and uninstalled

judgment.rationale: The reporter's clarification refutes treating this as demonstrated settings loss. The installer has its own CmdPal registration action, so disabled runtime state is not an uninstall preference. First settle whether manual package removal is meant to persist across bundle upgrades; a conditional servicing direction is reasonable, but no settings-reset repair or implementation-ready selective-install design is established.
evidence: The sequence is explicit: disable Command Palette, uninstall its package, then update PowerToys.

The author already answered the maintainer's /bugreport request with an archive and explicitly said the setting stays disabled. Waiting on the author or requesting the same report again would be wrong.
The supplied archive's general settings confirm CmdPal=false, supporting the distinction between package installation and module enablement.

proposed_fixes.title: Separate package-install preference from CmdPal runtime enablement
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: bundle registration runs during the new product's installation independently of the preserved CmdPal=false setting; this is servicing policy, not established settings corruption.
plan: Validate the package registration/disabled-setting sequence with existing diagnostics and a controlled upgrade.
Obtain installer/module owner agreement on persistent uninstall semantics; if supported, model that preference distinctly rather than suppress all servicing whenever the module is disabled.
Apply the agreed registration condition and cover upgrade, repair, fresh install, explicit re-enable, and per-user package state.
verification: A disabled module stays disabled after update.
The agreed package opt-out survives upgrade/repair as intended, while enabled/new installations still register and launch normally.

reproduce.title: Compare package servicing with a disabled CmdPal setting
reproduce.version_requirement: Reproduce the reported 0.102 upgrade path and a current stable-to-stable upgrade on an isolated account.
prerequisites: Use an isolated test account or controlled test machine; preserve existing user data.
steps: 1. Disable Command Palette and record the enabled flag, then remove only its registered package using the normal supported uninstall UI.
2. Upgrade PowerToys using the same GitHub installer channel and record whether the package is registered again while the enabled flag stays false.
3. Repeat a disabled-but-not-uninstalled control and an enabled control; inspect the incoming product's registration condition.
4. Have the installer/module owners decide whether separate manual removal is a supported persistent opt-out; do not silently reinterpret disabled as uninstalled.
reproduce.expected_result: Servicing behavior is documented and consistent; if persistent package opt-out is supported, it survives upgrade without blocking explicit re-enable or normal bundled servicing.
